title: The Ship Engineer
intro: Someone you met online works on a ship far away. He says he wants to visit you, but needs help first.
Tap anything that looks odd to sniff it closer. Pin what is suspicious, clear what is harmless.
When you are sure, decide what to do.

notify.text: I need $600 for my leave papers…

screen.context: You have been chatting online for four weeks. You have never spoken or met.

msg: My darling, my leave is approved! But the

msg.text: I love you, please do not let me down.

papers.label: Money for "leave papers"
papers.lens: A real employer handles its own paperwork.
papers.why: Needing money for papers is a classic story.

stuck.label: Salary "stuck"
stuck.lens: A reason why he cannot pay himself.
stuck.why: A reason that needs your money is a warning.

repay.label: "I will repay double"
repay.why: A promise to repay is bait.

where.label: "At sea, no network"
where.why: Being unreachable keeps you from checking.

actions.label: Say I will only help after we meet in person and a video call
Send nothing and report the profile

block_report.line: You sent nothing and reported the profile. It was removed.

verify.line: You asked for a video call and a name of his company. He had no answers, and the chat ended. Case cracked.

go_ahead.line: The $600 was lost. A "customs fee" and an "airport fee" followed.

what_if.go_ahead: Never sending money to someone you have not met, and asking for a video call, would have stopped it.
what_if.verify: Checking was smart. Reporting it as well helps protect other people.

golden_rule: Someone far away, working at sea or abroad, who needs money for papers is the classic romance scam. Send nothing.

quick_check.q: An online love interest says he is a ship engineer and needs $600 for leave papers. What do you do?

options.text: Ask him to send papers first

quick_check.explain: Working far away and needing money for papers is the classic story.

hints.nudge: Why can he not pay for his own papers?

rows.v: To someone you have not met
